segment: University and college foundations without a DAF programme (incl. foundations of government universities, foundation code 13)
can_sponsor_daf: yes (501(c)(3) public charity); public universities themselves no (170(c)(1) governmental unit) - use affiliated foundation
why_not_offering_today: Free alternative (accept grants from national DAFs); perceived demand low; 4966/4967 responsibility; reputational/host-benefit concerns; expertise
organizations_count_estimate: Higher-ed B40-B43/B50 >=$100M: 738 (50 with DAF signal); B11/B12 >=$100M: 380 (26); fc13 >=$100M: 167 (11); qualified core ~600-800 after overlap (INFERENCE)
count_basis: IRS EO BMF 2026-11-09 joined to DAFRC panel and repo non-DAFRC harvest; computed 2026-11-26

segment: Hospital and health-system foundations without a DAF programme
why_not_offering_today: Low perceived demand; few planned-giving DAF specialists; health-system IT security procurement
organizations_count_estimate: E11/E12 >=$100M: 263 (10 with DAF signal); hospitals E20-E24 >=$100M: 1,459 (11) (operating assets)

segment: Community foundations (sponsorship view of SEG-002)
why_not_offering_today: Already offer DAFs: 375 of 394 T31 >=$50M in DAFRC panel; untapped only among very small CFs
organizations_count_estimate: T31 >=$10M: 712 (616 DAF signal); CoF 'more than 900' (undated); DAFRC 804 reporting DAFs FY2024

segment: United Ways and federated giving organizations (T70)
why_not_offering_today: Mixed; one-third of large ones already sponsor

segment: Regional and community banks (sponsorship view of SEG-003)
needs_sponsoring_partner: yes - affiliated charity or partner sponsor (RCF, NPT, community foundation) or distributor (SEI-TIFIN)
why_not_offering_today: Cannot sponsor; TPRM 5/5; existing sponsor relationships; distribution economics
organizations_count_estimate: 4,204 FDIC-insured; 1,006 report fiduciary assets; 251 with $1-100bn fiduciary assets

segment: Credit unions (sponsorship view of SEG-004)
can_sponsor_daf: no (federal CUs are federal instrumentalities; state CUs 501(c)(14); not 170(c)(2) - INFERENCE, counsel to confirm)
why_not_offering_today: Cannot sponsor; small balances; no member DAF demand found (2025-26 search)

segment: Trust companies (sponsorship view of SEG-007)
why_not_offering_today: Cannot sponsor; fiduciary/TPRM; affiliated sponsors exist (Bessemer)
organizations_count_estimate: ~60 national trust banks; state charters UNKNOWN nationally (CO 8; MA 14+2; CA 7)

segment: RIAs and wealth firms (sponsorship view of SEG-005/006)
why_not_offering_today: Cannot sponsor; custodian DAFs free; pending advisor-as-donor-advisor rule

segment: Religious institutions without a foundation (churches, dioceses, ministries)
can_sponsor_daf: yes in law (church is 170(c)(2)) but practice is a separate foundation
needs_sponsoring_partner: often host on faith sponsor (NCF, Signatry, diocesan foundation)
why_not_offering_today: Scale; expertise; tithes should stay direct (affinity guardrail)
organizations_count_estimate: UNKNOWN (churches not required to file); X11/X12 >=$10M: 148 (34 DAF signal)

segment: Corporate giving and employee-benefit platforms
why_not_offering_today: Channel crowded (Daffy for Work, Givinga, Morgan Stanley at Work, Benevity)

segment: Fintechs (consumer giving and wealth apps)
needs_sponsoring_partner: yes - must form or partner with a 501(c)(3)
why_not_offering_today: Sponsor formation cost; reputational risk

segment: Custodians
needs_sponsoring_partner: have affiliated sponsors (Fidelity Charitable, DAFgiving360, Vanguard Charitable)
why_not_offering_today: Already served

segment: Accounting and tax networks (CPA firms)
why_not_offering_today: No public evidence either way; independence constraints for attest clients (INFERENCE)

segment: Insurance carriers and financial-planning firms (incl. fraternal benefit societies)
why_not_offering_today: Sponsor relationship; distribution

segment: CU league and CUSO foundations (sponsorship view of SEG-014)
why_not_offering_today: Manual operations (INFERENCE); member demand absent

segment: Professional and alumni associations
why_not_offering_today: Scale; c3/c6 separation

segment: Host sponsors able to carry other institutions' branded programmes (existing CFs and national sponsors)
why_not_offering_today: Hosting exists (Columbus Foundation for Ohio Wesleyan; BNY CGF hosted GW and MSU until Dec 2024); appetite for a separate platform UNKNOWN
organizations_count_estimate: Subset of 804 CFs and 82 national sponsors; count of active hosts UNKNOWN

segment: Family offices (sponsorship view of SEG-008)
why_not_offering_today: Use national sponsors or private foundations

segment: Adjacent: charitable gift administration (gift annuities, charitable remainder trusts, pooled income funds) at charities, community foundations and universities
can_sponsor_daf: yes (issuer is normally a 501(c)(3) public charity)
why_not_offering_today: Not a DAF question: these organizations already run planned giving; the adjacency is selling them a second module (most outsource administration to PG Calc/Foundation Source or bank trust departments)
count_basis: No public count of CGA issuers located; ACGA survey not fetched (P3-GAP-FGJ005)

segment: Adjacent: comprehensive fiscal sponsors (Model A project hosts)
why_not_offering_today: Capacity and scale: most are small; DAF sponsorship is a separate programme with its own policies; no evidence of demand
count_basis: 2023 field scan mailing list; Fiscal Sponsor Directory

segment: Adjacent: grant and scholarship administration at community foundations and private/corporate foundations
can_sponsor_daf: partly (community foundations yes; private foundations no)
why_not_offering_today: Already served by grants suites (Foundant/SmartSimple/GivingData; Blackbaud); a DAF vendor adds no reason to switch
organizations_count_estimate: >3,350 organizations on the Foundant group platforms (vendor claim)

segment: Adjacent: endowment and restricted-fund pool accounting (university, hospital and community foundation unitized pools)
can_sponsor_daf: yes (institutionally related foundations are public charities)
why_not_offering_today: Endowment accounting sits in ERP/fund accounting and custodian systems; DAF is a donor product, not an accounting need
organizations_count_estimate: 657 NACUBO study participants ($944.3B); hospital foundations not counted

segment: Adjacent: employee giving and corporate philanthropy platforms
why_not_offering_today: They route donations through their own or partner charitable entities; buyers of vetting and disbursement services rather than of DAF administration
organizations_count_estimate: A handful of large platforms (Benevity, Bonterra, Blackbaud, Deed etc.)

segment: Adjacent: private foundation administration
why_not_offering_today: Different tax regime (excise tax, payout, self-dealing); dominated by Foundation Source and family-office/bank administration
organizations_count_estimate: not computed (derive from IRS BMF foundation codes)

segment: Adjacent: bank and trust-company trust administration
why_not_offering_today: Fiduciary regulation and entrenched trust-accounting cores (FIS, SEI, SS&C)

segment: Adjacent: escrow and 1031 qualified intermediaries; other custodial accounting (UTMA, client trust accounts)
why_not_offering_today: Not charitable; state bonding/licensing; different buyers

segment: Adjacent: community investment and impact-investing programmes at foundations (loan funds, impact notes)
can_sponsor_daf: yes (when run by a public charity)
why_not_offering_today: Loan servicing and securities law dominate; little ledger overlap beyond restricted balances
count_basis: Screening judgment; no public count fetched
